lead_profile_text: Already on STL seeking management: 5 years self-hosting, wife is Superhost, wants to step back
stl_goal: Hand off day-to-day management entirely and take it easy
property_situation: Experienced Airbnb host of 5 years with 2 properties (had 4), 60-80% occupancy, about £30k a year each; wife holds Superhost status. Analysed property is the 3-bed at 4 Willow Terrace. Talking to 3-4 management companies; targeting handover by end of November. Mortgage not discussed.
property_type: 3-bed house, currently operating as an Airbnb
primary_blocker: Wants proof of local Glastonbury performance (property count and example figures) before choosing among 3-4 operators; Zac could not confirm the local count on the call
language_signals: It's a success. We've developed it, except that now we just want to take it easy a bit
Let somebody else run it for us
I just want to know you can do it, really
I'd still like to know how many you have in Glastonbury
I'm currently talking to about 3 or 4 people to take over the business for me, so I'm kind of well-versed in how it works
I really want to speak to people who are in the area already

delay_signals.trigger_phrase: I'm currently talking to about 3 or 4 people to take over the business for me
delay_signals.context: Comparing multiple management companies; says some tell him 'we're going to move into the area' but have no Glastonbury properties; wants Glastonbury examples before deciding
delay_signals.timeline_given: End of November handover; follow-up due about 2 Oct (3 working days)

green_light_signals.trigger_phrase: now we just want to take it easy a bit. Let somebody else run it for us
green_light_signals.context: Opening statement of intent to hand over management; later accepted the fee: '15%, I think, is reasonable'
Answer to Zac asking about timeframe

meeting_flow.opening_phrase: I thought I'd start just by understanding a bit on your current situation and situation with the property, you know, an interest in short letting, and then we can go through the figures and go through our service if it lines up with what you're looking for.
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: Right, I see. Okay, right, well, that's good news because that kind of lines up with what we've projected here.
meeting_flow.income_intro: So what we're looking at is £58,000 of gross, which is what guests pay in total.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: I can go through how the management sort of works so you can see, you know, what it looks like once moved to a management company.
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: Anything else you want to go through, Steve, or ... as far as sort of time frames with this, Steve, you know, when you're sort of wanting to get this? You're looking to sort of end of November?
meeting_flow.close_phrase: I'll send you a bit of a sort of summary of everything we've spoken about. I'll send the figures as well and then I'll give some examples for you, yeah?

lead_responses.what_lead_said: how many properties do you have in Glastonbury currently?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: I'd have to check off the top of my head. We have about 70 that we manage in total, in different areas, so I'll have to have a look at exactly how many in Glastonbury specifically.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Okay. (asked again later: 'I'd still like to know how many you have in Glastonbury')

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I just want to know you can do it, really, and the way I know that is to see your figures on a property you have in Glastonbury.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: I can't share property figures because I'd be sharing another landlord's income without permission; showed a 3-bed Manchester case study instead (projected £57k gross, 73% occupancy, £233 ADR versus actual about £57k, 69%, £211, net about £36k), normally within 10% either way.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Later: 'if you could dig up some examples of ... houses, Airbnbs you have in Glastonbury. Could you send me those?'

lead_responses.what_lead_said: What percentage of your bookings come from Airbnb, Booking.com, construction workers, etc.?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Don't know the exact platform split but normally 20-40% of bookings are direct, property dependent (better for contractors and relocation).
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: You say there's not very many events in Glastonbury?

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Glastonbury is many events all year round, winter and summer. That's the beauty of it because it's just crazy town.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Explained direct bookings work best for long-stay or contractor guests; event guests tend to book on trusted platforms rather than directly.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Yeah, I kind of know how direct bookings work

lead_responses.what_lead_said: let's say you've got somebody who's directly booked with you, not through a platform ... the TV's not working. And it's a £500 television. ... whose insurance are you talking about, mine or yours?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Damage deposit for small items, Stayful's guest cover insurance for major damage, plus ID checks to flag known risks; platform bookings have platform cover.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: we get damage from 3-day guests and 1-month guests

lead_responses.what_lead_said: finding cleaners is hard ... All very hard in Glastonbury. In fact, the best ones you would come across will say we're not taking any more work on at the moment because we're so booked up.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: That's common everywhere; Stayful has an approved contractor database requiring Google review thresholds and short-let spec with supplies and linen in a price per stay, and tenders locally for the most competitive price.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Okay. All right, well, certainly if you could ... send me those examples

lead_responses.what_lead_said: 15%, I think, is reasonable. Do you charge VAT on that?
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: So it's 17%. 17.5%. Yeah, 18%. Okay, all right. I think that's good. I'd just like to see some examples.

conversion_gaps.gap: Deck errors: property labelled '4 The Terrace, Bellerby, Leyburn' and read aloud; Glastonbury demand framed as mainly festival week; fee slide shows £42,180 'income after fees' versus £30,357 forecast
conversion_gaps.evidence: Steve corrected the events point: 'Glastonbury is many events all year round'
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Check deck address, comps and net figure before the call; research local seasonality; corrections disclosed in the email and action plan

conversion_gaps.evidence: Steve: 'We get about 30 grand a year each'; Zac: 'that kind of lines up with what we've projected'
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Frame the net (about £30,357) as the same income with the workload removed, and quantify the roughly £9,400 a year cost against his time

zac_language.numbers_framing: £58k gross, then the standard deductions (platform commissions, cleaning, 15% management), then a Manchester 3-bed case study showing projected versus actual
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Concedes honestly (cannot confirm local count, cannot share figures), then redirects to a general process answer; promises to follow up with examples rather than closing on the call

what_they_focused_on: Damage on direct bookings and whose insurance applies
what_they_needed_most: Local proof that Stayful can operate in Glastonbury
Evidence the handover will not take long to settle
Reassurance that damage and cleaner cover are handled
what_fell_flat: Manchester case study as a substitute for local proof
Framing Glastonbury demand as mainly festival week
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For experienced hosts comparing operators, lead with local proof (property count, anonymised local examples, named local cleaner capacity), position the sale as time back rather than extra income, and ask who else they are talking to
